A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, Figures 1–6, and Appendices A–E. The conference reformatting does not prevent matching the scientific content.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original particle and PDE simulations, including cluster formation and average exit times. Appendix C.6 reports additional Wasserstein-distance simulations.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C.6 retain these original simulation results, including particle trajectories, density evolution, repeated-run exit times, and clustering-distance curves.

M1.justification: The SA/USA particle dynamics and analyzed mean-field procedure are retained. Removing the extra 1/N in USA-MF aligns its expression with the unchanged particle equation and Eq. (3); it does not introduce a different implemented procedure. Nonidentity-matrix extensions are discussed but not implemented.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same synthetic circle-based particle dynamics, perturbed uniform densities, and clustering scenarios. The new discussion of BERT cites earlier work rather than reporting an additional evaluation.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an empirical comparison against competing methods. Newly cited work, including Sinkformers, is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains 10,000 particles at beta = 5 and 7, the same Euler timestep, and the same PDE grid and Lax–Friedrichs discretization. The beta = 2 exit-time experiment retains N = 1,000–16,000 and the 100-bin total-variation stopping procedure.

E4.justification: The temperature and particle-count analyses are retained. Appendix C.6 also retains the comparison of alpha = 0.01 and 0.001 supporting Assumption 3; no new ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 20 simulations per particle count for the exit-time experiment. Repeated-run information and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged, with no added seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The simulation plots are identical: beta = 5 and 7 produce three and four clusters, exit times show logarithmic dependence on N, and the Appendix C.6 curves agree after a time shift. No empirical result entries or findings change.

T1.justification: Section 2 removes the extra 1/N from the USA-MF integral. Remark 4.1 changes the stated coefficient from (k²/beta)I_k(beta) to I_k(beta)/beta and adds the assertion k_max ≈ sqrt(beta) as beta grows. The principal theorems, assumptions, and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: Introduction contribution 3 replaces persistence over 'exponentially long time intervals' with intervals of length O(ln N), substantially narrowing the claimed timescale. This corrects the contribution summary to match logarithmic scales already present in v1's formal results; the other central contributions remain stable.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds specific applicability qualifications concerning absent MLP layers and identity query/key/value matrices. It discusses possible matrix relaxations, MLP-dependent changes to the dynamics, and the relationship to reported BERT behavior. V1 mainly presented alternative matrices and training as future directions.

D1.justification: The code pointer changes from user837591937549230/metastable_transformers to gbruno16/transformers-metastability. Numerical implementation, PyTorch double precision, and Tesla T4 disclosures remain unchanged. The PDFs establish a changed access address, not changes to the hosted code.

R1.justification: V2 adds Sander et al. (2022), Agazzi and Lu (2021), and Cowsik et al. (2024), and removes the separate reference to 'The emergence of clusters in self-attention dynamics.' It revises model attribution and describes Geshkovski et al. (2024) as addressing complementary, well-separated configurations.

P1.justification: V2 tightens introductory and related-work prose, adds notation explanations in Section 4.2, corrects the exit-time figure reference from Figure 4 to Figure 3, and updates affiliations and citation style. The section sequence and most technical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reset into ICLR format, changing typography, headers, text width, captions, and equation-number placement. Figures are resized and repositioned; Figure 3 becomes a smaller figure with surrounding text. All six figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: V2 corrects the introductory timescale overstatement and inconsistent formulas, and adds concrete limitations on applying the simplified model to full transformers. These changes improve precision and interpretation. The central proofs and simulation evidence remain essentially unchanged, and Assumption 3 remains unresolved, so the overall improvement is limited.
